tagline: One take. Everything you need to sell it.
sector: Product photography studio moving from a day rate practice to a fixed price productized service
founded_place_size: Founded 2020 in Portland, Oregon. Three people: Nina (art direction and shooting), plus a retoucher and a studio assistant.
about: FOLD & GRAIN shoots small brands' products the way those brands actually sell them, in a row, as a range, rather than one hero at a time. For six years we sold days. We are now selling a product: one continuous take per client and, out of that single take, the shot board, the short films and the platform cuts a small brand needs to launch. Our work sits behind pantry goods at eight dollars and sterling silver at a hundred and eighty, and the whole point is that the same method tunes to each. Precision, repeatability and honesty about what a shoot can and cannot yield are the studio's stock in trade.
audience: Small and independent product brands (pantry, personal care, jewellery, homeware) launching or refreshing a web store and needing a full range shot to look like one afternoon. Founders who buy a fixed price and a fixed turnaround, not a day rate.
price_positioning: Repositioning from roughly fifteen hundred dollars a day to a fixed twenty two hundred to thirty five hundred dollars per client run. Mid-market, productized, premium to a freelancer but well under an agency.
typography: A clean neo-grotesque for headings and the studio wordmark, paired with a monospaced face for technical specs, parameters and captions on the service page. Type is set tight, quiet and utilitarian.
voice: Direct, specific, no salesmanship. We name what a shoot can deliver and what it cannot, and we write our recipes so an assistant could run them. Sentences are short and concrete.
brand_assets_status: FOLD & GRAIN has a consistent working look built up over six years but never a codified system. There is a set wordmark and studio colours in practice, no written guidelines. This engagement, which includes the studio's own service page, is where the identity gets formalized for the first time.
values: Repeatability over one-off flourish, honesty about limits, and price-appropriate craft: a treatment right for one band is wrong for another, and saying so is the service.
